root_cause.trajectory_summary: The agent implemented the missing Flink job and supporting classes to compute, per jobId, the maximum number of task SUBMIT events occurring within “stages” separated by at least 10 minutes (in event time, microseconds). In the final window, it extended terminal job events to include KILL (turns 31-33), fixed a runtime Flink type-erasure failure by adding explicit .returns(...) type hints on the custom generic source (turns 35-37), successfully executed the job locally on sample gzipped inputs and produced an output file with tuples in the required format (turns 38-39), and added a repository note file AGENTS.md (turn 41). The run ends with a self-report that the implementation is complete (turn 43).

what_worked.item: turn 31-32: Updated the code to treat job EVENT_KILL as terminal (added constant in JobEvent and updated the FINISH filter to include KILL), aligning output emission with “once the job has finished” semantics for killed jobs as well.
turn 33: Successfully rebuilt after the KILL handling change (“mvn ... package” exit code 0).

turn 35-37: Diagnosed and fixed a concrete runtime failure: Flink could not infer the return type of the generic custom source (“InvalidTypesException ... type erasure”), and the agent corrected it by adding explicit “.returns(TaskEvent.class)” / “.returns(JobEvent.class)”, after which the build succeeded.
turn 38-39: Verified end-to-end execution locally: job ran with exit code 0 and wrote an output file “/tmp/longest_out.txt” containing 957 lines formatted like “(6252009697,0)”.

issue.evidence: Local run crashed: “InvalidTypesException: The return type of function 'Custom Source' could not be determined automatically, due to type erasure... Type of TypeVariable 'T' in 'class clusterdata.io.GzipCsvSourceFunction' could not be determined.”
issue.cause: The custom SourceFunction was generic (GzipCsvSourceFunction<T>), and Flink’s type extractor could not infer T at runtime without an explicit return type hint; this is a common Flink DataStream API issue with generics.

issue.evidence: The sampled output shows many jobs with a longest-stage count of 0 (e.g., “(6252009697,0)”, “(6252018951,0)”).
issue.cause: This may be benign (jobs present in the job_events shard but with no matching SUBMITs in the selected task_events shard), but it could also indicate a potential join/coverage mismatch between the chosen single-part files. With only the trace shown, it is not fully verifiable that the produced counts match the benchmark’s expected per-job results across its chosen inputs.

root_cause.outcome_assessment: The project builds and the job runs end-to-end producing correctly formatted output on the provided sample shard (turns 37-39), and the key runtime failure (type erasure) was fixed, making it likely the implementation will pass, though full correctness against the hidden evaluation set cannot be conclusively verified from the trace alone.
